messages.subject: CFA with multiple ordinal item types - WLSMV appropriate estimator?
parts:
Hi,
       I'm having some trouble psychometrically validating a scale using CFA. The scale comprises 22 negative social events, with 3 different item types for each event.

1. How likely it is to occur to them (Probability) – 7 point Likert, not at all likely... very likely
2. How bad it would be if it did (Magnitude) – 7 Point Likert, not at all bad... extremely bad
3. How long they would feel bad for (Duration) – 7 point scale from <1hr...<14 days

Sample size is 369 participants and EFA supported three latent factors with two factors (Magnitude and duration closely correlated). Some of the distributions are non-normal, some skewed positively and some negatively given the items ask about magnitude and duration.

CFA and minimum reproducible CFA code with Data is attached below. Given three different item types, there are two models. Model 1 is simply the three factors, model 2 is a bifactor model, with three additional factors to account for each item type. For some reason, mag and dur items load very poorly on latent factors in the CFA model (in spite of good fit indices for the overall model).
My questions are:
1) given the skew and non-normality of the item distributions, and different item types, I chose WLSMV which has considerably better fit than MLR, is this appropriate?
2) if I use WLSMV is the standard RMSEA, SRMR, CFI, and NNFI fit indicies appropriate or should I use alternatives given we are not using ML?
3) Is the model specification as a bifactor model OK given the research aims?

Thanks in advance for any assistance!

These are the fit measures obtained for the two models specified below.



```{r}

Data <- read.csv("Data_min.csv", fileEncoding="UTF-8-BOM")
attach (Data)
```

```{r}

+ SCOPE_B16 + SCOPE_B17 + SCOPE_B18 + SCOPE_B19 + SCOPE_B20
+ SCOPE_B21 + SCOPE_B22  

Duration =~ SCOPE_C1 + SCOPE_C2 + SCOPE_C3 + SCOPE_C4 + SCOPE_C5
+ SCOPE_C6 + SCOPE_C7 + SCOPE_C8 + SCOPE_C9 + SCOPE_C10

Bad ~~ 0*Cost H

'
CFA.Model1 <- cfa(Model1, data = Data, estimator = "WLSMV")

Model1.fit <- fitMeasures(CFA.Model1, c("chisq", "df","pvalue", "cfi", "nnfi", "srmr", "rmsea", "rmsea.ci.lower", "rmsea.ci.upper"))
```

messages.subject: Re: CFA with multiple ordinal item types - WLSMV appropriate estimator?
parts:
I think your questions are better suited for SEMNET, given that they have nothing to do with particular software.

www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html
1) given the skew and non-normality of the item distributions, and different item types, I chose WLSMV which has considerably better fit than MLR, is this appropriate?

MLR returns basically unbiased results for 7-point scales

http://psych.colorado.edu/~willcutt/pdfs/Rhemtulla_2012.pdf
2) if I use WLSMV is the standard RMSEA, SRMR, CFI, and NNFI fit indicies appropriate or should I use alternatives given we are not using ML?

They are just as (un)informative with DWLS as ML estimation, but don't take suggested cutoffs too seriously:

http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/1094428110368562
3) Is the model specification as a bifactor model OK given the research aims?

Depends what you think the primary and secondary factors are.  You seem to consider probability, magnitude, and duration to be 3 separate constructs, but intuitively it seems the general factor is negative perception, measured by 22 events from a population of events/items you could have asked them about, and probability, magnitude, and duration are the method factors for assessing how negative something is. 

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
